takeaways: Equity markets are hitting record highs on AI-driven optimism, yet a widening divergence persists as bond markets signal skepticism over Fed credibility and the sustainability of overstimulated U.S. growth.

Global liquidity faces systemic risks as Japan’s currency intervention threatens to spill over into the U.S. Treasury market, complicating the 'higher-for-longer' interest rate environment for central banks.

Geopolitical and regulatory pressures are mounting on critical infrastructure, with potential bans on Chinese hardware and grid-connection audits forcing a costly, mandatory overhaul of data center supply chains.

items.title: All eyes on RBI as MPC meets amid rising inflation and global uncertainty
bullets: The Reserve Bank of India is expected to maintain its repo rate at 5.25% despite retail inflation climbing to 4.38% in June, breaching the central bank's 4% target for the first time in 17 months.
Rising food and fuel costs, compounded by geopolitical tensions in West Asia, are pressuring the MPC to adopt a more hawkish tone to manage price stability and support the rupee.
items.reason: Significant policy decision in a major emerging market facing inflationary headwinds.

items.title: Bond sell-off sent warning on Federal Reserve’s credibility, says top central bank official
bullets: A recent bond market sell-off has been interpreted by senior central bank officials as a direct signal of market skepticism regarding the Federal Reserve's commitment to its inflation-fighting mandate.

This development highlights growing investor concerns over the Fed's long-term credibility, potentially forcing a more aggressive policy stance to anchor inflation expectations and stabilize sovereign debt markets.
items.reason: Direct impact on global risk-free rates and central bank policy credibility.

items.title: Persistently high inflation to nag global economy, say economists: Reuters poll
bullets: Economists surveyed by Reuters indicate that global inflation is likely to remain sticky, complicating the path for central banks attempting to balance growth support with price stability.

The persistence of these inflationary pressures suggests that the 'higher-for-longer' interest rate environment may extend further than previously anticipated, impacting global capital allocation and corporate earnings forecasts.
items.reason: Broad macroeconomic consensus shift affecting global asset pricing.

items.title: S&P 500 set for first record high in two months
bullets: The S&P 500 is approaching a new closing record high, driven by a rotation into diverse sectors and a rebound in tech stocks that helped the index recover from a nearly 5% summer swoon.

Market sentiment improved significantly following comments from Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent regarding potential progress in negotiations to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which helped ease energy price volatility.
items.reason: Market-wide index performance and geopolitical de-escalation signals.

items.title: Why Palantir stock is ripping higher after earnings: AlphaSpace stat of the morning
bullets: Palantir reported a 149% year-over-year revenue growth in its US Commercial segment, signaling a decisive reacceleration in demand for its AI solutions that exceeded analyst expectations.

Management raised full-year revenue guidance to approximately $8.15 billion, an 82% increase over the prior year, while the stock's forward P/E ratio compressed to 84x, down from a four-quarter average of 199x.
items.reason: Significant earnings beat and guidance raise for a high-profile AI stock.

items.title: U.S. yen intervention signals perfect storm rising in FX and bond markets
bullets: The recent joint U.S.-Japan currency intervention, aimed at stabilizing the yen after it hit a 40-year low, highlights the risk of spillover volatility from Japanese Government Bond (JGB) markets into the $29-trillion U.S. Treasury market.

Japan remains the largest international creditor to the U.S. with $1.14 trillion in holdings, creating a systemic vulnerability where simultaneous stress in the yen, JGBs, and Treasuries could destabilize global financial liquidity.
items.reason: Systemic risk involving major sovereign debt holders and currency stability.

items.title: U.S. economy is overstimulated — and bond markets fear it
bullets: Nominal U.S. GDP grew at an annualized rate of nearly 8% in the second quarter, significantly outpacing the 25-year average and signaling potential overheating driven by fiscal policy and massive AI-related capital expenditure.

While corporate earnings have surged by nearly 50% for S&P 500 firms, the bond market is signaling concern through rising yields, creating a growing divergence between equity market optimism and fixed-income caution regarding inflation.
items.reason: Macroeconomic data indicating potential overheating and policy divergence.

items.title: How likely is Beijing to walk the talk on boosting consumption?
bullets: China's GDP growth decelerated to 4.3% in the second quarter, dragging the first-half average to 4.7% and leaving the economy barely within the official 4.5-5% annual target range.
The slowdown is characterized by a sharp 18% plunge in property investment and a significant cooling in retail sales growth, which dropped from 2.4% in Q1 to just 0.2% in Q2.
items.reason: Signals structural weakness and potential policy shift

items.title: More patient policy framework for China's economy
bullets: The economy is undergoing a structural transition toward an 'around 4 percent growth' era, as traditional engines like real estate and infrastructure are replaced by AI and advanced manufacturing.

Economic divergence is widening between industries and regions, creating a disconnect between official macroeconomic data and the actual financial health of households and local government balance sheets.
items.reason: Provides critical context on long-term structural shifts

items.title: HSBC resumes buyback after big profit jump in first half of 2026
bullets: HSBC reported a 27% increase in profit attributable to shareholders to US$14.6 billion, driven by growth in net interest income and higher fee income despite a US$2.4 billion charge for expected credit losses.

The bank is resuming a US$1 billion share buyback program and declared a second interim dividend of US$0.10 per share, signaling strong capital position and management confidence in its global restructuring strategy.
items.reason: Major capital return and strong earnings from a systemically important bank.

items.title: Hong Kong high street rents forecast to rise 3% this year
bullets: Retail sales in Hong Kong grew 10.6% year-on-year in the first five months of 2026, supported by a 14.1% increase in visitor arrivals, which reached 23 million during the period.
Colliers forecasts a 3% rise in high street rents for the year, constrained by limited prime retail space availability despite a more moderate growth pace expected in the second half.
items.reason: Indicates a modest recovery in the retail sector, a key component of the local economy.

items.title: Big Tech's Anthropic and OpenAI stakes are distorting the corporate earnings picture
bullets: Investment gains from private AI companies like Anthropic and OpenAI significantly inflated S&P 500 earnings growth, which would have been 29% instead of the reported 48% without these one-time equity revaluations.

Analysts warn that while these gains boosted headline figures, they mask the underlying performance of core software and service businesses, necessitating a non-GAAP approach to accurately assess corporate profitability.
items.reason: Highlights significant accounting distortions in major tech earnings reports.

items.title: Big tech to pay more if no deal reached with Australian media
items.source: ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation
bullets: The Australian government is increasing the potential levy on big tech companies to 2.5% of digital advertising revenue if they fail to secure commercial content agreements with at least six local news organizations.

Tech firms successfully negotiated a concession to apply the levy only to digital advertising revenue rather than total revenue, significantly limiting the financial impact of the proposed regulatory framework.
items.reason: Represents a shift in global regulatory pressure and potential margin impact for digital ad-heavy tech firms.

items.title: AI cloud startup Volta valued at $2.4 billion, announces $10 billion AI partnership
bullets: Volta has secured a $2.4 billion valuation, signaling continued investor appetite for specialized infrastructure providers within the capital-intensive AI cloud sector.
The firm has simultaneously entered a $10 billion AI partnership, representing a massive commitment of capital that underscores the rapid scaling of AI-specific compute resources.
items.reason: Significant capital deployment in AI infrastructure

items.title: America’s Cosmic Bet on AI
bullets: AI-related investments now account for 85% of all S&P 500 gains in 2026, highlighting an extreme concentration of market performance in a single technological sector.
With AI companies already representing over 40% of U.S. equity market value, upcoming trillion-dollar-plus IPOs from major players could push that concentration past the 50% threshold.
items.reason: Systemic market risk and concentration analysis

items.title: SK Hynix — Not Nvidia — Has Become the Most Important AI Chip Stock on the Planet
bullets: The AI hardware bottleneck has shifted from GPU design to high-bandwidth memory (HBM) supply, making SK Hynix a critical dependency for all major AI accelerator manufacturers.

Leveraged and inverse ETFs tied to SK Hynix now hold approximately $5.5 billion in assets, surpassing the exposure levels of both Nvidia and Micron, signaling a major shift in speculative capital flows.
items.reason: Identifies a critical supply chain bottleneck shift that is reallocating institutional capital.

items.title: The 1 Number Behind Nvidia’s Chip Scarcity That Most Investors Are Missing
bullets: Nvidia has disclosed $1 trillion in forward revenue visibility for its Blackwell and Rubin product cycles through 2027, providing the most concrete evidence of sustained, supply-constrained demand to date.

To support this backlog, Nvidia has ramped up supply-related commitments to $145 billion, confirming that the company is aggressively scaling inventory to meet hyperscaler demand despite ongoing production constraints.
items.reason: Quantifies long-term revenue visibility and supply chain commitments for the sector's most important stock.

items.title: Leapmotor Tops 100,000 Monthly Deliveries for the First Time
bullets: Leapmotor achieved a significant milestone by delivering 101,267 vehicles in July 2026, marking a 102% year-over-year increase and the first time the startup has surpassed the 100,000-unit monthly threshold.

Despite this record performance, the company has only reached 45.8% of its 1 million vehicle annual target, requiring a sustained monthly average of over 108,000 units for the remainder of the year to succeed.
items.reason: Significant growth milestone for a major Chinese EV player with clear implications for annual guidance.

items.title: EV sales outpace ZEV Mandate trajectory again as groups warn against policy changes
bullets: UK battery electric vehicle (BEV) registrations reached a 27.4% market share in July, consistently outperforming the effective ZEV mandate trajectory of 24.6% when accounting for industry credit flexibilities.

While BEV sales remain robust, the broader UK automotive sector faces headwinds, with total vehicle production falling 7.5% in the first half of 2026, prompting industry calls for urgent industrial strategy reform.
items.reason: Highlights regulatory compliance dynamics and broader manufacturing sector challenges in the UK market.

items.title: Texas governor directs PUCT, ERCOT to audit all data centers seeking grid connection
bullets: Texas has halted the 'Batch Zero' transmission planning study to conduct a mandatory audit of all data center interconnection requests, signaling a shift toward stricter regulatory oversight for large-load users.

With over 474GW of connection requests currently pending—representing five times the state's peak demand—this audit will determine if projects are financially viable and capable of paying for their own infrastructure impact.
items.reason: Significant regulatory bottleneck for hyperscale expansion in a key US data center market.

items.title: EXCLUSIVE: Trump administration drafting ban on Chinese data center devices, sources say
bullets: The administration is reportedly preparing to restrict the use of Chinese-manufactured hardware within domestic data centers, a move that could force a costly supply chain overhaul for operators.

This potential policy shift highlights escalating geopolitical risks for data center infrastructure, likely driving up capital expenditures as firms are forced to pivot toward non-Chinese equipment providers.
items.reason: Potential for major supply chain disruption and increased costs for US data center operators.

items.title: Rocket Lab’s $8 Billion Iridium Acquisition Creates a Powerful, Profitable Space Stock in 2027
bullets: Rocket Lab is pivoting from a pure-play launch provider to a vertically integrated space services company, with the $8 billion Iridium acquisition expected to provide the recurring, high-margin subscription revenue necessary to offset heavy infrastructure spending.

Analysts project Rocket Lab will reach a critical financial inflection point in 2027, narrowing annual losses to approximately $24 million while achieving positive free cash flow as its launch business matures and satellite operations scale.
items.reason: Major M&A activity signaling a shift in business model and path to profitability.

items.title: Musk likely to face tough questions during SpaceX's first earnings call as a public company
bullets: SpaceX shares have declined by 50% from their June peak, reflecting investor skepticism regarding future growth prospects and the company's significant cash burn, which is expected to exceed $4 billion for the first half of the year.

The market is bracing for increased volatility as the initial lockup period expires, releasing over 800 million shares for trading, which will more than double the current float and test investor sentiment regarding the company's long-term valuation.
items.reason: High-stakes public earnings debut and significant share dilution event.
